definitions.explanation: A piece of playground equipment consisting of a long plank balanced at its center, on which two people sit at opposite ends and rise and fall alternately. From English "seesaw."

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}でシーソーに{乗|の}った。
examples.english: I rode the seesaw at the park.

examples.japanese: {妹|いもうと}とシーソーで{交互|こうご}に{上|あ}がったり{下|さ}がったりした。
examples.english: My sister and I went up and down in turns on the seesaw.

examples.japanese: {体重|たいじゅう}が{違|ちが}うと、シーソーはうまく{釣|つ}り{合|あ}わない。
examples.english: When the weights differ, a seesaw doesn't balance well.

notes:
A common piece of playground equipment, alongside {滑|すべ}り{台|だい} (slide) and ぶらんこ (swing). The word is also used figuratively for things that go alternately up and down, as in シーソーゲーム (a back-and-forth, see-sawing contest).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- シーソーに{乗|の}る: to ride a seesaw
- シーソーで{遊|あそ}ぶ: to play on a seesaw
- シーソーゲーム: a see-saw game (a closely contested, back-and-forth match)
